title.rendered: ZIMBA TOWN COUNCIL COMMENCES BLOCK MOULDING PROJECT,EMPLOYS LOCAL YOUTHS.

content.rendered:
Zimba Town Council has commenced the moulding of concrete blocks for sale as part of its efforts to enhance revenue generation and support construction activities within the district.
The council is currently producing 400 concrete blocks per day using the block making machine and concrete mixer procured from locally generated income.
The project is part of the commitment to meeting the growing demand for quality and affordable building materials in Zimba District and surrounding areas.
This initiative is expected to benefit individuals, contractors, businesses, and institutions undertaking various construction projects by providing reliable access to locally produced strong blocks.
In addition, the project is anticipated to contribute to local economic growth while creating a sustainable source of income for the council and local employment.
The local authority has since employed five local youths to help support the production of quality blocks.
Residents and other stakeholders are encouraged to take advantage of the availability of these blocks and support the council’s efforts to improve service delivery through innovative and sustainable income-generating ventures.
The council remains committed to promoting development and providing services that contribute to the growth and prosperity of Zimba District.

title.rendered: MAPATIZYA LAWMAKER HANDS OVER TWO KEY CDF PROJECTS TO THE COMMUNITY OF MANGONDA & ZIMBA WARDS.

content.rendered:
The Member of Parliament for Mapatizya Constituency, Emeldah Munashabantu, has commissioned key Constituency Development Fund (CDF) projects aimed at improving education, sanitation, and healthcare services in Zimba District.
The commissioned projects include a 1×3 classroom block at Siameja Community School constructed at a cost of K1,265,906.80 and an ablution block with a water reticulation system at Zimba Mission Hospital Mothers’ Shelter, constructed at a total cost of K600,000 under the 2025 CDF.
Speaking during the ceremonies, Hon. Munashabantu said the projects reflect the government’s commitment to taking development closer to the people and addressing pressing community needs.
She noted that the classroom block will provide a conducive learning environment for pupils who previously relied on inadequate facilities such as a church building, while the health infrastructure will significantly improve sanitation, hygiene, and access to clean water for expectant mothers.
Hon. Munashabantu emphasized that the lack of proper sanitation and water supply at the mothers’ shelter had long affected the dignity, health, and safety of women, adding that the newly commissioned facilities will help address these challenges.
Meanwhile, Council Chairperson Loveness Chigora reaffirmed the local authority’s commitment to effective service delivery and prudent utilization of public resources. Council leadership noted that CDF continues to play a critical role in transforming communities by funding projects that directly respond to local needs.
The Council also stressed the importance of promoting sanitation and hygiene, describing access to clean water and proper sanitation facilities as essential to public health and human dignity.
District Commissioner has urged the community, school management, and hospital staff to take ownership of the newly commissioned infrastructure and ensure proper maintenance for long-term sustainability.

title.rendered: ZIMBA TOWN COUNCIL INTENSIFIES SENSITIZATION ON REVISED CASH FOR WORK PROGRAMME

content.rendered:
Zimba Town Council, through the Department of Planning, is currently conducting an extensive sensitization programme on the revised Cash for Work initiative set to be implemented this year.
The team of officers has been engaging Ward Development Committees, traditional leaders, and councillors, emphasizing the importance of identifying community projects that will stand the test of time and deliver lasting benefits.
The revised Cash for Work programme introduces several changes from the initial phase. Notably, payments for beneficiaries will now be processed centrally to enhance efficiency and accountability.
The programme will run for a period of six (6) months, during which beneficiaries will be expected to undertake tangible and impactful community works.
Participants will continue to work for 8 hours per day over a period of 10 days, earning K60 per day, totaling K600 per beneficiary.
Recruitment of beneficiaries will now be conducted by the Council on a first-come, first-served basis across all zones. This process will be facilitated by the recently recruited data entry clerks.
Members of the community are therefore encouraged to identify and propose projects that will have a lasting impact, in line with the objectives of the cash for work in the district.

title.rendered: THE CONSTRUCTION OF MARTENITY AT MAPATIZYA CLINIC IS A MILESTONE TO IMPROVED MARTERNAL HEALTH CARE-DR.MILIMO

content.rendered:

Dr. Kayawa stated that the development represents a major physical transformation that government has delivered to the people of Mapatizya and surrounding areas.
She explained that the new facility will allow expectant mothers to stay closer to the health centre, ensuring safer deliveries and access to proper maternal care.
Dr. Kayawa further revealed that the maternity annex and mothers’ shelter will serve at least 10 rural health centres in the area, enhancing healthcare delivery across the district.
She added that the maternity annex is equipped with both an antenatal clinic and a labour ward, making it easier for medical personnel to provide timely and efficient care to expectant mothers.
Dr. Kayawa noted that the availability of these facilities is expected to significantly reduce cases of home deliveries, which often pose risks to both mothers and babies.
Meanwhile, Government, through the CDF, has constructed the mothers’ shelter, while On-Call Africa is currently undertaking rehabilitation works at Mapatizya Clinic to further improve healthcare services in Zimba District.

Mr. Mwala reiterated that the local authority remains open and ready to assist citizens and stakeholders in understanding procurement and project implementation processes.
He also assured contractors that preference will be given to locally based companies and suppliers in the execution of this year’s Constituency Development Fund (CDF) projects.

title.rendered: ZIMBA TOWN COUNCIL MONITORS CDF-SUPPORTED WATER PUMPS IN MULAMFU WARD

content.rendered:

A total of 20 water pumps were provided to help mitigate the effects of climate change by promoting winter farming.
The pumps are enabling farmers to produce crops such as maize, vegetables, and other agricultural products, thereby enhancing food security and improving livelihoods in the community.
During the monitoring exercise, officers from the Community Development Ms.Ndumwai Madabwali , Socio-Economic Planning Ms.Mainza Maambo and Public Health Mr.Thabo Sitali observed positive progress among the beneficiaries.
Some cooperatives have expanded their activities and have even purchased chickens after selling vegetables produced last winter , showing the economic benefits of the initiative.
Speaking during the visit, Siankope Zone WDC Zonal Chairperson, Ms. Kizito Munkombwe, said the cooperative is planning to continue with more winter farming activities shortly after the end of the rainy season.
“Their target to buy more livestock in the next two years from the few produces they will make from the winter production,” Says Munkombwe.
The initiative highlights the impact of the CDF programme in empowering communities and supporting sustainable agriculture in the district.

title.rendered: ZIMBA EYE CLINIC RECEIVES US$2 MILLION FUNDING FOR THE CONSTRUCTION OF A MODERNIZED  EYE CARE FACILITY.

content.rendered:
Zimba District has received a significant boost in the health sector after securing US$2 million in funding for the construction of a modern double-storey eye care facility at Zimba Eye Clinic.
The project has been made possible through a partnership between International Vision Volunteers and Eye Surgeons International, with financial support from the Fiat Lux Foundation.
The project, which will be implemented by the Fiat Lux Foundation, is expected to be completed within 24 months and will greatly improve access to specialized eye care services for people in Zimba District and surrounding areas.
Speaking during the Ground Breaking Ceremony held at Zimba Mission Hospital today, Zimba District Commissioner Robinson Mulamfu said the construction of the state-of-the-art eye care facility aligns with the Government’s vision of ensuring that quality healthcare services are accessible to all citizens.
Mr. Mulamfu noted that access to eye care remains a critical need in many communities and emphasized that the new facility will play an important role in improving the wellbeing of residents in the district.
Meanwhile, Zimba Town Council Director of Health Dr. Milimo Kayawa said the new facility is expected to serve an estimated 120,790 people through the 16 health facilities spread across the district.
Dr. Kayawa expressed confidence that the project will strengthen health service delivery and bring specialized medical services closer to the people of Zimba.
And Southern Province Health Director Dr. Calistus Kayunga, in a speech delivered on his behalf by Provincial Clinical Care Specialist Clive Band, said the installation of specialized treatment equipment at the facility will make it unique within the province and position it as an important centre for eye care services in Southern Africa.
Dr. Kayunga added that the project will help strengthen the health system and contribute to the country’s efforts to achieve equitable access to quality health services as Zambia moves towards universal health coverage.
Speaking at the same event, President of Eye Surgeons International Dr. John Bosett said the facility will be equipped with modern technology that meets international standards and will also serve as a training centre for doctors and other eye care specialists.
Dr. Bosetti stressed that the advanced equipment to be installed at the facility will enable the provision of high-quality eye care services to the community.
Other notable leaders present at the event included Chief Sipatunyana’s representative Victor Sindowe, Zimba Town Council Chairperson Madam Loveness Chigora, Council Secretary Lubinda Mwala, Bishop Siachitema of the Pilgrim Wesleyan Church, International Vision Volunteers Medical Director Dr. Brighton Samoyo, Assistant Medical Director Dr. Muchoba Munyara, traditional leaders, Adam Bloom and Peggy Singer from Eye Surgeons International, as well as various heads of government departments.

title.rendered: GOVERNMENT APPROVES ELEVEN 2026 CDF  PROJECTS FOR MAPATIZYA CONSTITUENCY.

content.rendered:
The Government has approved eleven (11) Constituency Development funded Community Projects to be implemented in Mapatizya Constituency during the 2026 period, aimed at improving access to education and health services across the constituency.
In Simwatachela Ward, the education sector will benefit from the provision of desks at Kabanga Secondary School and other selected schools that enrolled Form One pupils in 2026 across the district.
The health sector in Misika will see the construction of a staff house, installation of water reticulation, development of a waste management facility, and the procurement of beds, chairs, and medical equipment at Misika Rural Health Centre.
In Mafumba Ward, the Government has approved the construction of a staff house, waste management system, and the procurement of beds, chairs, and medical equipment at Mafumba Rural Health Post.
After many years of waiting, Chuundwe Ward will witness the commencement of construction of a Rural Health Post, bringing essential health services closer to the community.
In Siamafumba Ward, a 1×3 classroom block will be constructed at Mooka Primary School, while Kanyanga Ward will benefit from the construction of a Rural Health Centre at Syejumba Village.
The education infrastructure drive continues in Mangonda Ward with the construction of a 1×3 classroom block at Sindowe Primary School, and in Zimba Ward with a 1×3 classroom block at Tore Shultz Primary School.
Further, Chidi Ward will benefit from a 1×3 classroom block at Simukanda Primary School, while Luyaba Ward will see the construction of another 1×3 classroom block at Kakopa Primary School.
This information has been issued by the Council Secretary, Lubinda Mwala, of Zimba Town Council.

title.rendered: ZIMBA PROPOSES CREATION OF ZIMBA CENTRAL CONSTITUENCY.

content.rendered:
Zimba District today held a District Delimitation Sitting at Zimba Secondary School, where stakeholders proposed the formation of a new constituency to be known as Zimba Central Constituency.
During the meeting, citizens submitted that the proposed Zimba Central Constituency should comprise the following wards: Zimba, Mangonda, Chuundwe, Luyaba, Kanyanga and Mafumba.
Stakeholders further proposed that Chidi, Siamafumba, Simwatachela, Mulamfu, Mbwiko and Chalimongela wards remain under Mapatizya Constituency.
Speaking during the official opening of the sitting, District Electoral Officer Mr. Lubinda Mwala emphasized that the delimitation exercise is a constitutional mandate being undertaken by the Electoral Commission of Zambia across all 116 districts of the country.
Mr. Mwala stated that delimitation of electoral boundaries is an essential component of a credible electoral process, as it ensures fair, equitable and effective representation in line with population growth and changing settlement patterns.
He noted that the legal foundation of the exercise arises from the Constitution of Zambia (Amendment) Act No. 13 of 2025, which increased constituency-based seats in the National Assembly from 156 to 226, thereby mandating the creation of 70 additional constituencies nationwide.
Mr. Mwala highlighted that Zimba District currently has a population of 109,307, with an annual growth rate of 3.7 percent based on the 2022 National Population Census, and is projected to reach 149,751 by 2032.
The DEO said this growth places increased demand on service delivery and representation, hence the importance of delimitation.
He clarified that all submissions made during the district sitting will be treated as proposals, subject to review and approval by the Commission. The process is expected to be concluded and the new constituencies gazetted by 15th May 2026, when Parliament stands dissolved.
Mr. Mwala urged stakeholders to engage transparently and inclusively, provide factual and data-driven submissions, and seek consensus wherever possible.
He further reminded stakeholders of the upcoming Inspection of the Provisional Register of Voters, which follows the conclusion of the Mass Registration of Voters on 29th November 2025.
Mr.Mwala encouraged citizens to take part in both the online and physical inspection exercises to verify their details and ensure the credibility of the forthcoming elections.
The District Delimitation Sitting forms part of a nationwide exercise aimed at strengthening Zambia’s democratic governance and enhancing equal representation for all citizens.

title.rendered: CONTRACTORS VISIT  THE PROPOSED CDF SOLAR PLANT SITE IN ZIMBA DISTRICT.

content.rendered:
A site visitation exercise for contractors expected to bid for the Presidential Initiatives Solar Plant to be funded using the 2026 Constituency Development Fund  in Zimba District has successfully been conducted.
A total of nine contractors repreesented their companies in visiting the earmarked project site as part of the pre-bid process. The proposed site is located opposite Dayow Beef Co. Limited (Abattoir).
The identified land is strategically positioned within a radius of 2.3 kilometres from the ZESCO Substation, which falls well within the recommended maximum distance of 5 kilometres for efficient power connectivity.
This makes the site technically suitable for the establishment of the solar power plant which will be feeding into the national grid in the district.
The solar plant project is among the key measures the Government has put in place to help address the power deficit currently being experienced in the country.
The project will be funded under the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) and is expected to contribute to improved energy security and sustainable development in the district.
Officers from Zimba Town Council who witnessed the site visitation included, Mr. Mattias Phiri – Director of Engineering,Ms. Annet Hamachili – Director of Planning,Mr. Obert Chivwanda – Senior Building Inspector and Assistant Director Mr.Sunday Nalumino.
Zimba Town Council remains committed to supporting national development programmes and ensuring that projects implemented in the district meet required technical and planning standards for the benefit of the community.

title.rendered: ZIMBA TOWN COUNCIL UNVEILS 2026 OUTPUT-BASED BUDGET ESTIMATES.

content.rendered:
Zimba Town Council held its ordinary council meeting on 30th December 2025, during which a number of key governance and development issues were discussed, including the financial outlook for the coming year.
Prior to the ordinary sitting, the Council convened a special full Council meeting to consider and adopt the 2026 output-based annual budget.
The budget was subsequently approved, marking an increase from K87,322,876 in 2025 to K88,945,664 in 2026. The increment has largely been attributed to increased allocations of the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) and other funding from the central government and donors.
Under the approved budget, CDF has risen from K36,058,151 in 2025 to K40,032,550 in 2026. Local governance allocation has also increased from K1,641,366 to K1,797,099, while integrated development planning has been allocated K1,687,933. Economic and business development will receive K42,435.
The Agriculture sector has been allocated K534,033, an increase from last year’s K459,034, while Livestock and Fisheries has received K503,176, up from K490,612. Health services recorded a significant boost, with an allocation of K6,351,370, representing a 100 percent increase from K3,200,587 in 2025. Meanwhile, social protection and community development has been allocated K17,960,467, reflecting a slight reduction from last year’s K18,193,033.
Both the special and ordinary council meetings were attended by all twelve councillors and heads of departments, underscoring the importance of the deliberations.
The 2026 output-based annual budget was presented by the Director of Finance, Mr. Martin Lindunda, who outlined the key changes and priorities aimed at enhancing service delivery and supporting local development in Zimba District.

title.rendered: GOVERNMENT COMMENCES ESTABLISHMENT OF A FARMER FIELD SCHOOL IN ZIMBA’S LIFALALE VILLAGE.

content.rendered:
The Government, through the Ministry of Green Economy and Environment, has commenced the establishment of a Farmer Field School in Lifalale Village of Mangonda Ward, aimed at mitigating the growing effects of climate change on agriculture, livestock, fisheries and forestry.
The initiative, which received K900,000 in funding in 2025, is designed to equip local farmers with practical, hands-on skills in agriculture, livestock management and horticulture.
The Farmer Field School is expected to serve as a key platform for promoting climate-smart agricultural practices and strengthening the resilience of farming communities against climate-related shocks.
Yesterday, a team of officers from the Ministry’s headquarters in Lusaka, accompanied by Heads of Government Departments from Zimba District, conducted a site inspection to assess progress on the project.
During the visit, the team observed the contractor installing and mounting a tank stand for a solar-powered water system that will support fish farming, livestock rearing and other agricultural activities at the facility.
Chief Sipatunyana welcomed and endorsed the project, urging the Lifalale community to take full ownership and actively participate in its implementation to ensure long-term success. He commended the Government for prioritising farmer training centres, especially at a time when climate change continues to disrupt conventional farming systems.
The Farmer Field School will feature an aquaculture demonstration through the construction of a fish pond, alongside practical demonstrations in livestock rearing, crop production and tree planting, to be supported by the Forestry Department.
Once fully operational, the facility is expected to significantly enhance farmers’ technical knowledge and capacity to adopt climate-smart farming practices, ultimately improving food security and promoting sustainable livelihoods in Lifalale and surrounding communities.

title.rendered: MULAMFU RURAL HEALTH POST, STAFF HOUSES AND WATER RETICULATION SYSTEM NEAR COMMISSIONING

content.rendered:
The Mulamfu Rural Health Post maternity annex, staff houses and water reticulation system are nearing commissioning following the successful completion of key remedial works aimed at making the facility fully operational.
This week, Council Secretary Mr. Collins Simoonga led a team of council officers alongside the Mapatizya Constituency Development Fund Committee (CDFC) Chairperson, Mr. Victor Sindowe, to inspect ongoing remedial works at the Mulamfu health facility. The project is being implemented with support from the Constituency Development Fund (CDF).

The remedial works include the completion of plumbing installations and connection of pipes to fully operationalise the water reticulation system within the maternity annex. In addition, new solar batteries have been procured and installed to enhance solar-powered lighting, ensuring reliable energy supply for the facility.

A multidisciplinary team comprising engineers, plumbers and electricians from the local authority has been stationed at the site for the past 14 days.

The team is working to ensure that all outstanding works are completed to the required standards and that the facility is ready for handover to the community.

Once commissioned, the Mulamfu Maternity Annex is expected to significantly reduce pressure on nearby health facilities, particularly Kabanga Rural Health Centre in Simwatachela Ward and Chidi Rural Health Centre in Chidi Ward, both of which are located approximately 15 kilometres away.

The long distance has previously posed serious challenges for expectant mothers and patients seeking medical services.
The completion of the facility will greatly improve access to maternal and general health services for residents of Mulamfu Ward and surrounding areas.

The official commissioning date will be announced in due course. Residents of Mulamfu Ward are expected to mark the milestone as the facility begins delivering much-needed health services closer to the community.

title.rendered: PRESIDENT HICHILEMA HIGHLIGHTS GOVERNMENT COMMITMENT TO UNITY, EDUCATION AND DEVELOPMENT IN 2026.

content.rendered:
President Hakainde Hichilema has reaffirmed his commitment to serving the people of Zambia, stating that he intentionally chose public service because of his love for the Zambian people.
Speaking during a community engagement, President Hichilema said his Government will continue taking care of citizens and called for unity and mutual care among Zambians.
He cited Free Education as a key indicator of his Government’s love and commitment to the people, adding that the delivery of desks to schools under the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) is another demonstration of care for communities across the country.

President Hichilema added that his Government has constructed palaces for traditional leaders, built houses for chief retainers, and provided motorbikes to support traditional governance structures.
Looking ahead to 2025, the President said there is a need to increase investment in the drilling of boreholes and construction of schools under the CDF, in order to further improve access to essential services.

He said the Act will promote proportional representation, thereby strengthening inclusiveness in the country’s democratic system.
The President was speaking during a rally held at Choma Sports Club on Wednesday.
Zimba Town Council Chairperson Madam Loveness Chigora and District Commissioner Mr. Robinson Mulamfu were among the dignitaries in attendance.

title.rendered: NAKOWA MATERNITY ANNEX COMMISSIONED AND HANDED OVER TO THE COMMUNITY.

content.rendered:
Nakowa residential area in Zimba Ward has received a major boost in maternal healthcare following the commissioning of the Nakowa Maternity Annex by Mapatizya Member of Parliament, Hon. Emeldah Munashabantu.
Speaking during the commissioning ceremony, Hon. Munashabantu said the new facility marks an important milestone in improving access to safe and quality maternal health services for women in Nakowa and surrounding communities.
She explained that the maternity annex will help decongest Zimba Mission Hospital by bringing essential maternity services closer to the people, thereby saving time, reducing costs, and ultimately saving lives.
Hon. Munashabantu revealed that the facility is fully equipped with a water reticulation system and solar power, ensuring uninterrupted service delivery.
She urged the community to take ownership of the facility and protect it from vandalism, emphasizing that it belongs to the people and will benefit current and future generations.
She further stated that the project was made possible through the enhanced Constituency Development Fund (CDF), which she said has enabled the government to address historical development gaps in previously neglected communities. The MP assured residents of Nakowa that more development projects are still in the pipeline for the area.
During her address, Hon. Munashabantu also announced that CDF funds have been allocated to improve the water supply at the mothers’ shelter at Zimba Mission Hospital.
Additionally, she disclosed that funds amounting to K 800,000 have been allocated to the Southern Water Supply and Sanitation Company to extend water services to Treasure Compound as part of efforts to address long-standing water challenges.
The Nakowa Maternity Annex was constructed at a cost of K1.5 million, while the accompanying water system, which will also benefit the surrounding community, cost K270,000.
Hon. Munashabantu attributed the visible development in Mapatizya Constituency to responsible leadership under President Hakainde Hichilema and strong collaboration with local leadership. She called on the community to work together in safeguarding public investments to ensure they continue to improve people’s lives.
The commissioning ceremony was attended by the District Commissioner, the Council Secretary was represented by Director health services, traditional leaders, senior government officials, health personnel, members of the press, and residents of Nakowa and nearby areas.

title.rendered: CDF BRINGS JOY TO KAMUKKEZA VILLAGE AS 60 YEARS WITHOUT A HEALTH FACILITY COMES TO AN END.

content.rendered:
The Government has officially handed over a maternity annex in Kamukkeza Village, bringing relief to residents who for many years were forced to walk over 20 kilometres to access maternal health services.
The facility was commissioned by Mapatizya Member of Parliament, Honourable Emeldah Munashabantu, and is expected to serve a population of about 6,000 people.
Hon. Munashabantu described the maternity annex as a gift to the people of Kamukkeza Village, noting that the community is among the settlers who were relocated to pave way for the construction of the Kariba Dam decades ago. She said the project demonstrates the Government’s commitment to addressing historical challenges faced by marginalized communities.
Meanwhile, Zimba Town Council Chairperson, Madam Loveness Chigora, urged the community to safeguard the facility against vandalism, emphasizing that it had taken many years for the area to acquire such an important health infrastructure. She further reaffirmed the Council’s commitment to delivering quality primary health services through its health department.
District Commissioner Robinson Mulamfu commended Government for remembering the people of Kamukkeza Village through the Constituency Development Fund (CDF). He said CDF projects in Zimba District are being implemented in needy areas in a manner that appears almost miraculous due to their impact on people’s lives.
Zimba Town Council Secretary, Mr. Collins Simoonga, also praised the community for working closely with the local authority to ensure the successful completion of the project.
Several government officials, political leaders, and community members attended the commissioning ceremony, which marked the handover of the first-ever health facility in Kamukkeza Village.
The maternity annex was constructed at a total cost of K2,099,616.03 under the Constituency Development Fund (CDF).

title.rendered: ZIMBA’S TREASURE COMPOUND SET TO BENEFIT FROM K800,000 CDF WATER PROJECT

content.rendered:
Southern Water and Sanitation Company in Zimba district has been funded through constituency Development Fund to implement a long-awaited water supply project in Treasure Compound, an area that has experienced chronic water shortages for decades.
Mapatizya Member of Parliament, Hon. Emeldah Munashabantu, today graced the ground-breaking ceremony for the project, which is scheduled to commence this month.
The scope of works includes the laying and connection of water pipes, installation of a booster pump, construction of a tank stand, and erection of a 10,000-cubic-litre water tank. The pipeline will run approximately three kilometres from the main treatment plant to Treasure Compound and is expected to benefit about 8,000 residents.
The project will cost K800,000 and will be implemented over a period of 60 days. As part of community involvement, Zimba Town Council has recruited 30 local residents to take part in excavation and backfilling works along the pipeline route.
Speaking during the ceremony, Hon. Munashabantu described the project as a major milestone and the beginning of a lasting solution to the water challenges that Treasure Compound has faced for many years.
The Member of Parliament was accompanied by CDF Chairperson Mr. Victor Sindowe, Ward Councillor Cllr. Anne Mutunda, and other community leaders.

title.rendered: ZIMBA COUNCIL LAUNCHES A PLANT FIVE  FRUIT TREES INITIATIVE AT HOUSEHOLD LEVEL

content.rendered:
The Department of Agriculture services at Zimba Town Council has rolled out an ambitious “Plant a Minimum of Five Fruit Trees” initiative aimed at strengthening food, nutrition, and income security while promoting a greener environment.

The programme was officially launched by the District Commissioner (DC)Mr.Robinson Mulamfu who was represented by the District Agriculture Officer (DAO) Mr.Lishomwa Mwendabai.

In his keynote address, the DC underscored the importance of the initiative, noting that fruit-tree planting will enhance community resilience against the adverse effects of climate change while contributing to afforestation and reducing deforestation in the district.

He further urged the local authority to mainstream the planting of at least five fruit trees in all Constituency Development Fund (CDF) projects and other construction works undertaken within the district.

The DC also appealed to traditional leaders to champion the initiative by ensuring that every household under their leadership plants fruit trees.

Council Chairperson Madam Loveness Chigora echoed the significance of the programme, stating that the practice of planting fruit trees is not only environmentally beneficial but also supported biblically. She said the initiative will broaden nutrition sources for the general public and create opportunities for income generation. The Council Secretary shared similar sentiments, emphasising the long-term community benefits.

Representing Chief Sipatunyamana, Mr. Sindowe reaffirmed the commitment of the traditional leadership to work closely with the government and the council to ensure the initiative takes root in both Sipatunyana and Simwatachela chiefdoms. He highlighted the critical role parents play in instilling tree-planting habits in their children to secure a greener future.

The initiative is expected to contribute significantly to environmental sustainability and improved livelihoods across the district as households and institutions embrace the culture of fruit-tree planting.

title.rendered: ZIMBA TOWN COUNCIL SUCCESSFULLY RELOCATES GRAVES  TO PAVE WAY FOR TAMBAANA DAM EXPANSION

content.rendered:
The Department of Heath at Zimba Town Council has successfully exhumed and relocated graves that were situated within the construction radius of the expanding Tambaana Dam in Sibooli Village, Simwatachela Ward.
Scores of residents gathered to witness the solemn exercise, which included traditional rites such as the sprinkling of traditional beer and the performance of incantations in honour of the deceased.
Government, through the Council, has been in close consultation with the family of the late Titus Sibagwe Munkombwe, who died 26 years ago. His grave, along with those of two children, was exhumed and relocated to allow for the expansion of the dam wall.
General workers from Zimba Town Council led by the Senior Health Inspector Mr Thabo Sitali and Community Development Officer Mr.Jackson Mbewe played a key role in the physical exhumation process, which commenced at around 13:00 hours. The Zambia National Service (ZNS) supported the operation by providing an excavator to ease the work of the Council team.
Government is increasing the dam wall height from the current 6.5 metres to 12.5 metres to support enhanced water retention for the community.
The event was attended by District Commissioner Robinson Mulamfu, Council Chairperson Madam Loveness, Area Councillor Cllr. Tobias Keenabanyama, and a representative from the office of the Member of Parliament, Mr. Charles Chikobela.

title.rendered: ZIMBA TOWN COUNCIL HOLDS FULL COUNCIL MEETING

content.rendered:
Zimba, October 30, 2025 — Zimba Town Council today held its Full Council Meeting in the Council Chamber to deliberate on key developmental programmes and Government policy initiatives aimed at fostering sustainable growth and enhancing service delivery across the district.
The meeting commenced with a moment of silence in honour of the late Mr. Ackson Sejani, former Chairperson of the Local Government Service Commission and former Member of Parliament for Mapatizya Constituency, in recognition of his distinguished and selfless service to the nation.
In her address, Council Chairperson Madam Loveness Chigora urged Councillors and stakeholders to actively mobilize residents for the ongoing mass voter registration exercise, emphasizing the importance of civic participation in strengthening democracy.
She further called for unity of purpose in achieving district development goals and underscored the need to expedite the implementation of Constituency Development Fund (CDF) projects while ensuring strict monitoring and accountability to prevent misuse of empowerment grants.
Meanwhile, Council Secretary Mr. Collins Simoonga reported that most 2025 CDF projects are currently under procurement. He also acknowledged reports of defective boreholes in some wards and assured the meeting that corrective measures are being undertaken to ensure all works meet the required standards.
Mr. Simoonga announced that the township roads have been graded to a distance of 7 kilometers, covering sections from the railway line along the T1 (Lusaka–Livingstone Road) to the Agriculture Offices, the Level Crossing to Treasure Compound, and from T1 to Muzya Stream. Works on Muzya Road have so far covered an additional 6 kilometers.
He further added that the local authority completed works on the Ackson Sejani Road, linking Mapatizya Road through to Kabanga Market, covering a total distance of 87 kilometers.
Providing an update on the agricultural sector, District Director of Agriculture Services Mr. Duncan Nyirongo informed the meeting that Zimba District received 8,525 input packs under the Farmer Input Support Programme (FISP), of which over 1,300 have already been redeemed. He cautioned agro-dealers against exploiting farmers and appealed to Councillors to report any cases of malpractice.
The Council reaffirmed its unwavering commitment to transparency, accountability, and inclusive development, reiterating its dedication to improving the welfare and livelihoods of all residents in the district.
The ordinary Council meeting was attended by His Royal Highness Chief Sipatunyana, Heads of Government Departments, Councilors, and community representatives.

title.rendered: ZIMBA DISTRICT DEPLOYS VOTER REGISTRATION OFFICERS AND UNIFORMED OFFICERS AHEAD OF MASS EXERCISE

content.rendered:
Zimba District has deployed Assistant Voter Registration Officers (AROs) in readiness for the commencement of the mass voter registration exercise scheduled to begin tomorrow, 13th October 2025.
The deployment exercise was witnessed by District Voter Registration Officer Mr. Collins Simoonga and Uniformed Officer Supervisor Mr. Bristol Choongo, who oversaw the distribution of 12 AROs (Field), 12 uniformed officers, and 12 registration kits across the district.
Mr. Simoonga said the deployment marks an important step in ensuring that all eligible citizens in Zimba District are captured during the voter registration period. He emphasized that the exercise will also cater for new registrations, transfers, and replacement of lost or damaged voter’s cards.
During the first phase, each registration team will be stationed at their designated polling stations for four days before moving to the next location. One kit has been left at the Zimba Civic Centre, where registration will continue throughout the exercise.
The deployment plan for the first four days is as follows:
Chidi Ward – Simundivwi Primary School
Luyaba Ward – Luyaba Secondary School
Mangonda Ward – Muzya Primary School
Mafumba Ward – Mafumba Primary School
Mulamfu Ward – Siankope Community School
Siamafumba Ward – Mukamba Primary School
Kanyanga Ward – Masanzya Primary School
Simwatachela Ward – Kabanga Basic School
Chalimongela Ward – Chalimongela Primary School
Zimba Ward – Makoli Primary School and Zimba Basic School
Mbwiko ward will be registered in the second phase and the kit will be stationed at Mbwiko Primary School.
Further,the Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) has set 30th April 2026 as the cut-off date for eligibility, meaning that any citizen who turns 18 years old on or before that date is eligible to register as a voter.
Zimba District is targeting to register over 45,000 voters during this mass registration exercise.

title.rendered: CHIDI WARD HEALTH POST OFFICIALLY HANDED OVER TO GOVERNMENT

content.rendered:
In a landmark development for rural healthcare, On Call Africa has officially handed over a newly constructed health post in Chidi Ward, Zimba District, to the Government of the Republic of Zambia. The health post, built at a cost of K2.5 million, was formally handed over during a ceremony held earlier today.
The handover event was officiated by Southern Province Assistant Secretary Mr. Bestone Mboozi, who represented the Provincial Minister, Hon. Credo Nanjuwa. Delivering the keynote address, Mr. Mboozi commended the initiative as a crucial step toward bridging the healthcare gap in rural communities.
“This infrastructure is a testament to the government’s commitment to improving healthcare delivery in underserved areas,” Mr. Mboozi said. “It reflects our shared vision of ensuring that no one is left behind in accessing quality health services.”
He further called on the local community to take full ownership of the facility and protect it against vandalism, noting that the health post is a lasting investment meant to serve both current and future generations.
The Chidi Health Post is poised to transform healthcare access for over 11,258 residents across 11 zones. It is expected to enhance the delivery of primary healthcare services, particularly in maternal and adolescent health, and significantly reduce travel distances for patients seeking medical attention.
Speaking at the event, On Call Africa Chief Executive Officer Mr. Nkandu Chikonde reaffirmed the organization’s dedication to complementing government efforts through infrastructure development and the strengthening of rural health systems.
Mr.Chikonde says the organization has also donated 17 bicycles to communicate based volunteers( CBVs) who will be supporting the health post on health care services in the villages around the health post.
The ceremony drew participation from several high-profile dignitaries, including Zimba District Commissioner Mr. Robinson Mulamfu, Kazungula District Commissioner Mr. Elias Siamibila, Council Secretary Mr. Collins Simoonga,Director of Health Services Dr. Milimo Kayawa, Provincial Health office and Presidential Delivery Unit and Chidi ward councillor Cllr Ivan Seemani.
Traditional leadership was also present, with Mr. Mate Sichibeya representing Chief Simwatachela and Chief Musokotwane of Kazungula District in attendance—highlighting the strong collaborative efforts that made the project possible.
The new Chidi Health Post stands as a beacon of progress and partnership, promising to uplift healthcare standards and transform the health outcomes of rural populations in Zimba District and beyond.

“This project is a testament to what we can achieve when resources are managed effectively as a team and with the people in mind,” She said.

title.rendered: ZIMBA TOWN COUNCIL PRESENTS THE 2025 BUDGET

content.rendered:
Zimba Town Council Secretary Mr. Collins Simoonga has officially presented the proposed budget estimates of revenue and expenditures for the year 2025, at the ongoing national budget hearing for local authorities.

The principal officer made the budget presentation amounting to K,87,070,380 this afternoon at the Lusaka Legacy resort in Chongwe district ,where 21 local authorities are gathered for the budget hearing.

The budget outlines how K 21.9 million will be channeled towards CDF Community Projects such as construction of infrastructures and grading of roads in Mapatizya Constituency 6.2 million Youth and Women Empowerment, another K 6.2 million has been allocated to both Secondary boarding School and Skills development bursaries in order to enhance quality education and reduce illiteracy levels within the district.

Further, Local Governance program has received an allocation of K1.6 million, while K153,517 will be channeled towards the community engagements, the Integrated Development Planning has been allocated K1.6 million, Economic and Business Development has received an allocation of K498,222, Public Health and Environment protection will be funded a sum of K430,639.

The total budget estimates for Zimba Town Council has increased by 67 percent from last year’s K 60 million due to the increased CDF allocation from K30.6 million to K36.0 million, also an increment of Devolved Function Grants from 460,328.93 to K18.7 million, an increase in the Cash For Work program and the Zambia Devolution Support Grant from World bank which has also increased from K3.7 million to K8.3 million.

The ongoing National budget hearing for local authorities was held in Chongwe, Kabwe and Mpika districts from 9th to the 13th of December,2025.

title.rendered: GOVERNMENT DRILLS FIVE CLIMATE RESILIENCE BOREHOLES IN MAPATIZYA CONSTITUENCY

content.rendered:
The Government through Zimba Town Council has intensified the drilling and equipping of climate resilient industrial boreholes funded under the 2024 constituency development fund in Mapatizya Constituency.

The local authority has successfully drilled five out of eleven boreholes earmarked to be drilled in strategic parts of the Constituency as part of the climate resilience measures that the government has lined up in addressing the drought impact experienced during this year’s rain season.
This year, the Ministry of local government and rural development directed local authorities to use 50% and 100% of 2024 Condtituency Development Funds empowerment and disaster components respectively, in responding to the climate change effects.
Chilubwa village in Simwatachela ward was the first beneficiary of an industrial borehole after it stayed for over thirty years without a functioning water facility.
Other places that have already received the boreholes are; Gala village in Chidi ward,Chalinga village in Mafumba ward, Siamutwezuba School in Siamafumba ward and Siayuni village of Luyaba ward.
In Chuundwe ward, a dry borehole was recorded despite the contractor making twice attempts at a depth of 134 mitres and 100 mitres.
However ,the Fabrication of tank stands to be installed in all the boreholes with siayuni village being installed right now ,while Masanzya school has a borehole that has been upgraded to solar powered.
Under climate resilience projects,Mapatizya Constituency is expected to receive six new boreholes,four upgrades on existing boreholes and one procurement of the engine pump for an irrigation facility.

title.rendered: ZAMBEZI RIVER AUTHORITY GIFTS ZIMBA’S NJABALOMBE COMMUNITY A HEALTH POST.

content.rendered:
The Zambezi River Authority has handed over Njabalombe rural health post to the government of the republic of Zambia the community to start receiving medical services within the locality.

The new health facility will be an addition to the eight already existing rural health posts across the district of a population of about 108,000 people.

Permanent Secretary in charge of technical services at the Ministry of ENERGY ,Mr.Peter Mumba officiated the highly attended event held in Njabalombe this afternoon,and stated that the construction of the health facility aligns well with the 8th national development plan which is targeting to improve health care services in the country.

Mr.Mumba who is also a Co-Chairperson at the Zambezi River Authority board says the project is a testimony of a good working relationship between the government and the private sector.

He commended Zambezi River Authority for pumping $152,000 in putting up such a facility for the community,adding that the government is pleased to learn that a total of 13,000 households will benefit from the same facility.

Southern Province health director Dr.Clive Banda who was also present at the event ,revealed that the new rural health post is expected to serve 10% of the entire population of the district.

He says this project will be a step in the right direction as the ministry aspires to have an improved provision of medical services to the people.

Meanwhile, Zambezi river authority director of Projects and Dam management Mr. Sithembinkosi Mhlanga says the authority will continue supporting people that were displaced during the construction of Kariba dam in 1960 through responding to some challenges that they facing.

Mr.Mhlanga says the health posts construction by the ZRA, will include outpatient and inpatient departments,marternity annex ,2 staff houses and 32 bed admission ward.

He advised the community to write down more projects that they feel should be worked on by his organization to the council.

And both Mapatizya member of Parliament Emeldah Munashabantu Nkhata and Zimba district commissioner Robinson Mulamfwu commended the government and ZRA for the continued support rendered to the community.

 

The two leaders were among the dignitaries that were in the entourage of the permanent secretary at Njabalombe today.

Others who attended the event include, Chief Simwatachela’s representatives Mr.Mate Sichibeya ,Zesco and REA officials,councilors and heads of government departments.

He emphasized the need to motivate health workers through confirmations and promotions in order to enhance health care services in the Ministry.
The Minister further revealed that the government is making plans to install solar power systems at all health facilities across the country in order to address power outages caused by load management.
Dr.Muchima further requested civic leaders to support the health practitioners working in various rural health centres so that they deliver for the people especially that the new dawn government has put health care services as the first priority.
He has since assured the nation that the government is fully stocked up to date with essential drugs to serve the citizenry.

title.rendered: GOVERNMENT INJECTS OVER K200, 000 TO ADDRESS WATER CRISIS AT ZIMBA SECONDARY SCHOOL

content.rendered:
Government has injected K240,000 to drill a 200-meter-deep industrial borehole at Zimba Secondary School, aimed at resolving the water crisis that threatened to disrupt the second term.

The project has been financed through the 5% disaster component of the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) to address sanitation challenges at the school and create a healthy learning environment for students.

According to District Commissioner and Chairperson of the Disaster Management Committee, Mr. Robson Mulamfwu, the government responded promptly to the situation after witnessing the struggles of pupils who had to walk long distances outside the school boundaries to access safe and clean water in residential areas.

Mr. Mulamfwu commended the Mapatizya Constituency Development Committee for facilitating the allocation of funds to resolve the situation at the secondary school. He added that surrounding communities will also benefit from the drilled water facility, while the government continues to seek funds to drill more industrial boreholes in Treasure, Malambo, and Namadula areas.

Zimba, a district in Southern Province with a low water table, has seen few industrial boreholes succeed in supplying water to households in the urban area, making this intervention crucial for the community.

He explains that effective actualization of the policy, requires a clear definition of roles and relationships of institutions involved to avoid duplication and conflict.
Mr.Mr.Hamulyata says decentralization is a program that involves changes in power relationship between central and local levels of government.
The Provincial Local Government Officers-PLGO says a Successfull implementation of the decentralization policy is dependent on political will from councilors and other politicians in order for the citizens to embrace and understand the devolved power , responsibility and resources.
Mr.Hamulyata emphasized that government demands a serious and honest approach in implementing Constituency Development Funded Projects in all wards based on the people’s needs.
The training is also being attended by the Council Chairperson Ms.Loveness Chigora, Council Secretary Mr.Christopher Siasinyanga , Heads of Departments and other members of staff.

content.rendered:
Environment Africa Zambia has dedicated today’s commemoration of International Day of Children’s in launching the installation of boreholes, bathing shelters for girl-children and VIP Toilets in Zimba District.

Environment Africa WASH officer Mr. Haggai Mendai says the sanitary facilities that the organization is putting up in Zimba symbolize its commitment to creating a child-friendly community that values the rights and well-being of the young people.

The Organization has been working in five wards of Zimba district namely Mbwiko, Chalimongela, Simwatachela, Luyaba and Mangonda with special attention to improving Agriculture, sanitation, environment protection, children’s rights and climate change.

Zimba District Commissioner Mr. Robson Mulamfwu graced the occasion and emphasized the need to protect the rights of children as government has placed great importance on the walfare of the young people in the district.

He further spelt out the government’s commitment to protecting children’s rights through the implementation of various policies such as the introduction of free education, distribution of desks and the construction of classroom blocks under the Constituency Development Fund-CDF.

In a speech read on her behalf by Mapatizya Primary School Headteacher Mr. Orbit Munanku, Zimba District Education Board Secretary Ms. Inonge Rita says today’s commemoration of children’s rights should act as a wake up call for the country to serious consider the rights of the young people.

She said pupils and the entire Mapatizya Primary School and community were having difficulties in accessing clean water, but the coming of the water system funded by the Environment Africa will help improve sanitation at the school.

Zimba District today joined the rest of the world in commemorating the international day of children rights commemorated under the theme ” RENEWING OUR PROMISE FOR CHILDREN’S RIGHTS where all Heads of government Departments,Zimba Town Council, Traditional leaders and other stakeholders gathered at Mapatizya Primary School to commemorate the day.

title.rendered: ZIMBA COUNCIL SENSITIZE OVER 200 PROPERTY OWNERS ON RATES PAYMENTS

content.rendered:
Zimba Town Council has successfully engaged members of the community on the importance of paying rates for the properties that they own in the township.

Council Secretary Mr. Christopher Siasinyanga, who spoke during the meeting which was called to interact and sensitize the community, emphasised on the need to pay property rates housed in the district.

Mr.Siasinyanga says there have been misunderstandings of each other between the council and the community, regarding the payment of certain rates to the council.

The Principal officer expressed happiness with the level of interaction that both the community and the council management had during today’s meeting.

He has called for continued engagement and collaboration between the council and the community to enhance service provision.

“Am very excited to see several property owners coming to this meeting where we will educate one another on the need to pay Property rates to the council, this interaction should not only end here but also continue after this sensitization meeting” ” says Mr Siasinyanga

And Zimba Town Council Treasurer Mr. Sandona Luzendi, advised property owners to always engage the council on any challenges that they encounter in making payments of rates and levies.

He said the non-payment of rates and levies to the council is a deterrent to the provision of services such as road maintenance, garbage collection and others.

    Zimba Town Council councilor Ms.Anne Mutunda speaking during the sensitization meeting


Speaking at the same event, Zimba Ward Councilor Ms. Anne Mutunda says the fact that the district is slowly transiting from rural to urban, there is need to follow the provisions of the law in putting up structures.

She says there is a need to seek guidance from the local authority on any structure that one plans to establish to help the council have well-planned residential and commercial areas.

Over two hundred property owners in Zimba district attended the meeting and appreciated the sensitization on the Rating Act No. 21 of 2018 and pledged to comply in payments of property rates.

title.rendered: SOUTH FARMERS CAUTIONED AGAINST SELLING AGRICULTURAL INPUTS

content.rendered:
The Ministry of Agriculture in Southern Province has launched the redeeming and distribution of farming inputs under the Farmer Input Support Program – FISP for the 2023/2024 farming season.

Speaking during the launch held in Zimba today, Southern Province Agriculture Coordinator Dr. Maxwel Choombe, says the government has put up serious measures to prevent farmers from selling or sharing farming inputs that will be distributed under the Farmer Input Support Program-FISP.

Dr. Choombe, says no farmer will be allowed to share or sell their inputs as doing so will lead to serious punishment such as being deregistered and blacklisted from the beneficiaries list.

He has called on farmers in the province to ensure planting the certified seeds and not recycled ones as it is the sure way of having better yields next year.

“In Southern Province, the recommended variety of seed is medium and Early maturing, let us make consultations with agriculture experts in your areas and ensure that we plant the right seed,” Says Dr. Choombe.

Dr. Choombe further advised farmers from the Gwembe Valley to focus on planting early-maturing varieties due to the low rainfall patterns that are expected to be experienced in the region.


And Zimba District Commissioner Mr. Rabson Mulamfwu, says the government will be delighted to see farmers that will collect inputs fully participate during the 2023/2024 Farming Season.

Mr. Mulamfwu has since assured farmers in Zimba, that the government through the Food Reserve Agency – FRA will prioritise the buying of maize from farmers who are on the FISP list.

He has urged farmers to ensure that they practice conservation farming as they prepare for next year’s farming season.

“Early land preparation is key to better yields, let us ensure that we practice conservation farming during the forthcoming farming season,” Says Mr. Mulamfwu.

Meanwhile, Zimba Council Chairperson Madam Loveness Chigora, says the early distribution of inputs is a fulfilment of the UPND government’s campaign promise.

She has appealed to the Ministry of Agriculture to consider increasing the number of FISP beneficiaries in Zimba due to the growing number of small-scale farmers.

A total number of 7, 653 farmers are expected to benefit from the Farm Input Support Program – FISP in the Zimba district.

Mr. Mulamfwu has advised the beneficiaries of loans and grants to undertake the businesses and help government realise it’s vision of having an economically stable nation.

Dr. Kayawa stressed that failure to prevent diseases in the district does not only affect health but also has an impact on social-economic factors in the district.
Meanwhile, Chief Sipatunyana’s representative Mr. Victor Sindowe has appealed for intensive support from the traditional leaders, churches and other government departments in sensitizing the people on the importance of polio vaccinations.
He says the traditional leaders are always ready to help spearhead any government agenda aimed at helping the subjects.
Zimba District Health Office will from today embark on the polio vaccination exercise where health officers will be conducting door-to-door campaigns across the district.
The district has had three rounds of vaccination campaigns that captured a number of children both in rural and urban areas.
The fourth round polio vaccination exercise in Zimba district is targeting total number of thirty six thousand four hundred and thirty four (36,434) Children that are below the age of eight years.

Zimba Town Council plans ahead to ensure no one is left behind…
Accurate and accessible geospatial data plays a pivotal role in district planning for Zimba District, Zambia, where planners are trying to facilitate development. Through an interview with Josephine Chiila, District Planning Officer in Zimba, we learn how GRID3 population, settlement and infrastructure data are being used to identify service provision gaps and inform future development decisions.
